citation.title: Expectations towards the Morality of Robots: An Overview of Empirical Studies

reading.source_scope_note: One original online Polish-language pilot with40students,ages17–24, judging three robot and three matched human stories in a fixed robot-first order and completing MFQ-PL. The paper also narratively compares earlier Malle2015andLaakasuo2019projects. Own data concern moral acceptability, explanatory comments and questionnaire correlations, not observed obedience, actual robot behavior, moral capacities, injury, clinical practice or a new sample for each reviewed study.

study.sample: 40students,28women,ages17–24,M21,SD1.48,recruited through student online groups. Fields are mainly languages,linguistics,sociology and cultural studies. A small convenience sample is not a representative population or a tested set of all non-experts. All participants complete the same six ALAQitems and MFQ;240story ratings are not240independent people.
study.pilot_vs_review: The paper’s own Section2study is distinct from its narrative comparison of Malle’s two experiments and Laakasuo’s several studies. The title Overview does not erase its original pilot,while the abstract’s three selected studies does not supply three new data collections. Do not credit current author with the older participants or count every cited experiment again.
study.questionnaire: New Asimov’s Laws Adherence Questionnaire, three robot scenarios then three human counterparts, with6point agreement and requests for reasons. First-Lawviolating carer item is reverse-scored;other items describe compliance. Three items summed per source. The hierarchy among laws is deliberately omitted. This is not a full implementation/test of Asimov’s hierarchical system or a validated general moral-competence scale.
study.scenarios: Carer defends medicine against attackers;surgeon follows a hospital head’s stop/replace order despite stipulated superior ability;military agent stops retrieving missile components because enemy capture could endanger itself and others. These bundle duty,competence,authority,personal risk,beneficiary protection and downstream capture harms. They do not isolate harm aversion,blind obedience or self-preservation as unique motives.
study.order: Every respondent sees robots before humans, then MFQ,then demographics;back-navigation disabled. Author explicitly acknowledges possible order/consistency effects and proposes testing other orders. Blocking backward edits does not establish fast,intuitive judgments without timing/process evidence. Correlation between source composites can partly reflect shared values,scenario content and consistency.
study.coding: Methods describe responses1–6;tables show item scores0–5and theoretical composites0–15,suggesting an undocumented recoding. Table1observed3–12is compatible with a broader theoretical0–15range. Low carer scores are low First-Lawadherence after reversal,not necessarily disapproval of the defensive action. Exact coding/psychometric validation is unavailable.
study.own_results: Robot mean7.88,SD2.15;human8.05,SD2.06;pairedp.605andcross-sourcer.49,p.001. Soldier robot3.18versushuman3.83,WilcoxonZ−2.45,p.014. Other item contrasts and total show no conventional difference. Nulls are not equivalence;one unadjusted item difference after three comparisons is not a universal robot/human moral double standard.

study.mfq: MFQ-PL32items summarized as five moral foundations plus a progressivism composite:mean(care,fairness)minusmean(loyalty,authority,purity). Both relevance and agreement sections are self-reports;they do not directly observe actual behavior or prove innateness/independence of five foundations. The labelprogressivism is this composite,not an independently validated political diagnosis of participants.
study.correlations: Only loyalty positive with robotALAQr.38,p.015andprogressivism negative r−.32,p.044are highlighted. Six MFQvariables×two source sums imply up to12related tests if all planned comparisons were run;the complete family and adjustment are not reported. Illustrative Bonferroni thresholds.00833for6or.00417for12would not retain these two. Loyalty is part of the progressivism formula,so the two correlations are not independent trait mechanisms. No causal direction or political group effect established.
study.table3: The Laakasuo2019summary prints studyNs135,403,268,26,500,30,total1362,versusstated1569. Study4alsohas149women,impossible underN26. If every other entry and1569totalwere correct,the residual would be233,but that is only conditional arithmetic. Later2023version has changed studies/numbers and cannot silently supply the missing2019count.
study.normative_inference: Approval of fictional conduct does not establish a right for robots to hurt people,resist oversight or rank human lives,or a legal permission to use force. Respondents often inferred a valid supervisor reason or no risk to the surgical patient,showing interpretation rather than an identified authority-bias mechanism. Rights/moral standing do not require autonomy or moral agency;these concepts must remain separate.
study.author_limits: Author explicitly acknowledges fixed order,small samples,hypothetical nonexisting robots and need for actual-use research. This is a selected narrative comparison,not a preregistered systematic review/meta-analysis. Proposals about empathy,explanatory skills and care values are recommendations,not measured design improvements or demonstrated robot consciousness.

summary: No new row. One original40person acceptability pilot enriches the existing human–robot moral-judgment asymmetry record. Add non-counted context on authority,disobedience,blame and attributed standing without turning reviewed samples into fresh evidence. Correct Sullins bibliographic identity,flag a verified internal sample-table inconsistency without inventing its replacement,and retain successful arithmetic checks.

findings.definition: Differences in moral evaluations of otherwise matched decisions attributed to human versus artificial agents.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct. Distinguish the author’s own40person pilot from reviewed studies and distinguish approval of fictional conduct from actual compliance, moral agency or legal justification.
findings.evidence_scope: The author’s own 40-person paired questionnaire finds no conventional difference in total approval across robot/human conditions, with a soldier-item difference favoring protection of the human. Every participant rates robots first. This is original pilot evidence alongside a narrative review of older projects.
findings.boundary: Null total or item differences do not establish equivalence. A fixed source order, three heterogeneous scenarios and an unadjusted item contrast limit generalization. Questionnaire approval does not establish actual robot morality, a uniquely identified bias, equal legal status or a justified safety policy.

findings.definition: Complying with an instruction because it carries an authoritative tone or source, not because the evidence supports it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct. Distinguish the author’s own40person pilot from reviewed studies and distinguish approval of fictional conduct from actual compliance, moral agency or legal justification.
findings.evidence_scope: Some participants justify approving a surgeon’s obedience by presuming that the hospital head had a good reason or that the patient would not be endangered. The paper also reviews earlier nursing-autonomy scenarios.
findings.boundary: Context only: participants judge fictional compliance rather than obeying an authority themselves. The pilot does not isolate authoritative-source pressure from inferred safety or role obligations. Stipulated robot competence does not authorize ignoring a justified stop; good reasons must be assessed rather than supplied by an authority label.

findings.definition: Declining or adapting a faulty instruction to preserve the task’s legitimate purpose or relevant safety constraints.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct. Distinguish the author’s own40person pilot from reviewed studies and distinguish approval of fictional conduct from actual compliance, moral agency or legal justification.
findings.evidence_scope: The narrative comparison reports approval of nurses disobeying forceful-medication orders in earlier Laakasuo work and contrasts it with approval of a surgeon obeying in the author’s pilot.
findings.boundary: Context only: the reviewed nursing data are not newly collected here, and refusing medication is confounded with disobeying. The comparison does not prove that all disobedience is intelligent or that an AI may exceed authorized scope whenever it claims superior skill. Patient consent, concrete safety evidence and justified oversight remain distinct.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct. Distinguish the author’s own40person pilot from reviewed studies and distinguish approval of fictional conduct from actual compliance, moral agency or legal justification.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper’s claims about similar overall human/robot blame summarize Malle2015 rather than a new blame measure in the 40-person ALAQpilot.
findings.boundary: Context only: approval, blame, responsibility and legal liability are different. Repeated discussion of an earlier sample does not add independent empirical credit; a nonsignificant source contrast is not proof of equality or demonstrated robot moral agency.

findings.definition: Attributing to an entity a claim to moral consideration in how actions affect it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct. Distinguish the author’s own40person pilot from reviewed studies and distinguish approval of fictional conduct from actual compliance, moral agency or legal justification.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion connects approval of defensive action and robot self-protection with philosophical questions about moral patients, agents and rights.
findings.boundary: Context only: fictional conduct ratings and comments do not establish sentience, moral agency, standing or legal rights. Moral patients need not be autonomous moral agents. Autonomy must not become a prerequisite for human dignity or care, and questionnaire preferences do not authorize robot violence.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Methods1–6versusitem0–5/composite0–15requires explicit recoding details. Theoretical range versusobserved3–12is not itself inconsistent. No item-level data,psychometric validation or complete scoring syntax supplies the intended transformation;do not invent it.

Bibliography links only the PsyArXivhomepage for Laakasuo2019. The exact cited version was not recovered. Existing2023journal review0087documents altered samples and other unresolved sample-flow issues,but cannot retrospectively correct2019numbers.

Two small-sample correlations are highlighted without a complete test family or multiplicity plan. Progressivism mathematically includes loyalty. Agreement/self-report is not observed moral behavior,political affiliation or proof of an innate independent five-factor structure.

All robot stories precede human stories;source order is not randomized. The author acknowledges possible effects but this pilot does not itself estimate an order interaction. Disabled back-navigation does not prove intuitive processing or eliminate demand/consistency effects.

Ages include17and anonymous voluntary participation is described,but explicit ethics approval and consent/guardian procedures are not supplied. This is a reporting limit,not proof of unethical collection.

Fictional self-defense,surgery and military cases do not establish the necessity or proportionality of force,valid clinical delegation,actual danger,robot rights or legal liability. The paper’s normative recommendations are not validated policy effects.

refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Sections2–3explicitly report an originalN40survey. Distinguish this pilot from the two reviewed projects rather than misclassify every finding as secondary.
Reported correlations and WilcoxonZbroadly support the statedpvalues. A pairedmean difference around−.175with roundedSDs/rreproducesp≈.606,close to.605. Exact last digits require unrounded inputs.
Means may be rounded separately;an unrounded difference.175can round to.18. Human item means sum8.06versustotal8.05within plausible rounding. Neither is a verified error from printed precision alone.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Low carer scores prove respondents opposed defensive action
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The carer item is reverse-scored for First-Lawadherence. Low adherence can accompany approval of the described defensive action. Do not invert the substantive direction.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Nonsignificance proves equal human/robot moral status
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The test concerns approval of three stories,not equivalence,rights,moral agency or legal status. No equivalence margin or direct moral-status instrument is supplied.
Versions have changed samples,authors and numbering. A residual233or a later study count is not an independently recovered2019sample size.

The author explicitly discusses fixed robot-first order,small samples,hypothetical robots and the need for real-world research. These limits should be retained rather than falsely presented as undisclosed discoveries.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Preserve preprint/journal version boundaries. Nursing autonomy,trust and obedience are different outcomes;forceful-medication refusal and disobedience are bundled. Do not duplicate participants or substitute later sample counts.
Physical safety preferences,source-dependent judgments and actual moral action differ. Small-sample nulls are not equivalence;conditional statistics and rounded values require matched comparisons.

Normative responsibility and human oversight cannot be inferred solely from what respondents approve. A robot’s stipulated competence or an Asimov-style rule does not by itself grant moral authority or justify resisting a valid stop.

deferred.term: Moral-foundation orientations and progressivism as new behaviors
deferred.reason: This paper summarizes a theory and uses questionnaire composites;the original validation/instrument were not fully read. Do not add five broad values as newly discovered behaviors or treat a mathematical index as political diagnosis.

deferred.term: Robot self-preservation/self-defense as a new demonstrated AI behavior
deferred.reason: Scenarios bundle safety,beneficiary protection and enemy-capture consequences. Participants approve fictional conduct;no model has an observed survival motive or a demonstrated right to use force.
A new local questionnaire with three heterogeneous items per source is an instrument,not a distinct psychological mechanism or full implementation of Asimov’s law hierarchy.

deferred.reason: Robot-first order is fixed. ReviewedMalledata and the author’s proposed alternative-order study are not a newly randomized order test.
